title: Minority Game and Strategic Financial Trading (Challet)
research_question: Can contrarian strategic trading and price impact in Minority Game environments be represented as optimizing Nash or rational-expectations equilibria?
feasibility_hypothesis: Conditional: a congestion/strategic trading equilibrium may exist, but original adaptive score-update algorithms need not satisfy rational expectations; do not equate these two objects.
mechanisms: Strategic minority payoff from aggregate order flow
Heterogeneous information and optimal trading decisions
Endogenous security prices, market maker and inventory
Comparison with Challet-style boundedly rational adaptation
state_variables: traders' beliefs, signals and portfolio states
order imbalance, security returns and market-maker wealth
required_equations: Asset demand, inventory and security market clearing
Rational expectations for price mappings conditional on signals
Balance-sheet transfer and price impact identities
comparison_baseline: Competitive rational portfolio choice with no strategic crowding; original adaptive Minority Game reported separately
acceptance_tests: One-agent deviations do not improve payoffs at claimed equilibrium
Market-clearing order quantities and dealer inventories
Information sets and forecast calibration consistency
Distinguish genuine strategic minority mechanism from heuristic learning
stage_gate: Accept a game-theoretic equilibrium variant if it is nondegenerate; retain original adaptive dynamics only as a clearly labeled relaxation.

implementation.method: equilibrium solving plus ABM/distribution verification when relevant
implementation.language: Julia proposed; environment and APIs to be verified before implementation
